title: Micron’s Numbers Show Why HBM4 Memory Is Worth 15X Its Weight In Gold
gist: Micron's fiscal Q4 2026 shows revenue up 4.8X to $54.23 billion at ~70% net margin, driven by price-led AI memory demand; HBM 2027 supply is largely contracted at higher prices and memory makers are deliberately limiting capacity growth through 2028.

insights.claim: Micron's fiscal Q4 2026 revenue rose 4.8X year on year to $54.23 billion, with operating income of $43.75 billion (nearly 12X) and net income of $37.7 billion (12X).
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Memory pricing power is producing margins rarely seen in hardware; Micron earnings are a read-through for the whole memory complex.
insights.locator: In the quarter, Micron's revenues went skyward

insights.claim: Micron converts 69.5 percent of revenue to net income, yet is deliberately not building memory and flash fabs faster than its already ambitious plan.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Capacity discipline sustains pricing; watch capex guidance as the signal for supply loosening.
insights.locator: Micron is bringing 69.5 percent of revenue

insights.claim: Micron's cash and investments reached $73.45 billion (up 7.6X year on year) against only $10.77 billion of capital expenditure in the quarter, enough to build nearly four fabs.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Huge cash pile gives optionality for buybacks, capex or M&A, but spending is constrained by fab build timelines, not money.
insights.locator: Micron has enough cash on hand

insights.claim: Micron guided fiscal Q1 2027 sales to $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion, about 13 percent sequential growth and 4.5X year on year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Guidance implies growth decelerating sequentially but still extreme year on year; compare against consensus.
insights.locator: As for guidance, Micron only talked about Q1 F2027

themes.theme: Segment economics: Cloud Memory and Core Datacenter

insights.claim: Micron's Cloud Memory unit (dominated by HBM) had $16.28 billion of sales in fiscal Q4, up 3.6X year on year and 18.3 percent sequentially, with 83 percent gross margin and 76 percent operating margin.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HBM-led segment margins exceed 75 percent operating, showing extraordinary pricing power.
insights.locator: In fiscal Q4, the Cloud Memory business

insights.claim: Micron's Core Datacenter unit (regular DRAM and flash) grew 11X year on year to a little over $18 billion, showing conventional DRAM and flash are core to AI clusters for training, inference and agentic AI.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: AI demand is lifting conventional memory and storage, not just HBM, widening the beneficiary set.
insights.locator: The Core Datacenter business was up 11X

insights.claim: Micron's total datacenter revenue rose 5.6X to $34.29 billion (35.6 percent sequential growth) with datacenter operating income of $27.68 billion, 81 percent of revenue.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Datacenter is now the dominant profit engine at Micron.
insights.locator: Add them together, and Micron's datacenter revenue

insights.claim: The author estimates Micron's HBM sales at $14.33 billion in fiscal Q4 (up 7.6X), high-capacity server DIMMs plus LPDDR at $8.05 billion (up 6.1X), and other DRAM at $17.39 billion (up 3.1X); Micron no longer discloses these segments.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: These are the author's estimates, not company data; HBM is the fastest-growing DRAM subsegment on this view.
insights.locator: My best guess has HBM memory driving

insights.claim: Across all products, Micron's DRAM bits shipped rose only a single-digit percentage in Q4 while prices rose in the high teens percent; flash bits rose 10 percent year on year with prices up 30 percent.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Growth is mostly price-driven, which is more fragile than volume if shortages ease.
insights.locator: Mark Murphy, Micron's chief financial officer

insights.claim: The author infers that price increases and shipments for HBM, LPDDR and high-end server DRAM were above the blended average, since no other explanation fits the datacenter numbers.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Suggests the mix shift toward AI memory is the key margin driver.
insights.locator: I think the price increases for HBM, LPDDR

insights.claim: DRAM sales rose 4.4X to $39.77 billion but flash was the fastest-growing line at 6.2X to $14.1 billion, even though DRAM remains far larger.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Flash is a catch-up beneficiary; NAND exposure may deserve attention.
insights.locator: The DRAM business rose by 4.4X

insights.claim: Memory makers believe the AI boom will last through 2028 at least and probably into 2030, and none want to build capacity fast enough to cause a bust, behaving like OPEC nations with oil.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A cartel-like supply response could extend the memory upcycle and lift peak-cycle earnings durability; the risk is a demand break.
insights.quote: They’re learning, like OPEC nations with oil.
insights.locator: Micron has enough cash on hand

insights.claim: Even if Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix could build and ramp a fab in a year, the author argues they might choose not to because unit memory prices keep rising.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Break from the classic boom-bust capex overbuild pattern is the key debate for memory multiples.
insights.locator: Even if Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix could build

insights.claim: Micron's CEO said calendar 2027 and 2028 memory and flash supply will be tighter than 2026; DRAM bit growth slows from mid-20s percent in 2026 to low-20s in 2027-2028, while flash bit growth rises from low-20s to mid-20s.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Tight supply through 2028 supports pricing; flash is easier and cheaper to expand than DRAM.
insights.locator: In general, Mehrotra said that memory and flash

insights.claim: Taller HBM stacks at higher speeds yield worse, so HBM4E and HBM5 will burn through more DRAM wafers on dud stacks than HBM4 and HBM3E, and yields will keep getting worse.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Yield loss consumes DRAM capacity, amplifying tightness in conventional DRAM as HBM generations advance.
insights.locator: Micron did say it would expand its capex in fiscal 2027

insights.claim: Micron said it will increase capex in fiscal 2027, aimed at raising DRAM output.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Watch magnitude of capex increase as the signal for the future supply response.
insights.locator: Micron did say it would expand its capex in fiscal 2027

insights.claim: Micron has completed agreements for the vast majority of its calendar 2027 HBM bit supply with significant year-over-year price increases, narrowing the HBM gross margin gap with conventional DRAM.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HBM margins converging up toward DRAM margins means HBM pricing is rising faster than conventional DRAM; 2027 HBM revenue is largely locked.
insights.quote: completed agreements for the vast majority of our calendar 2027 HBM bit supply with significant price increases year over year
insights.locator: Going forward in 2027, Micron is going to hike

insights.claim: Micron is working with Nvidia on the industry's first custom HBM4E implementation, NVHBM, to be adopted in next-generation GPUs and NVLink Fusion platforms.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Custom HBM deepens Micron-Nvidia ties and raises switching costs.
insights.locator: The HBM4 ramp, Mehrotra added

insights.claim: Micron customers have prepaid $32 billion for supply, Micron has 26 supplier agreements covering about 35 percent of revenue through fiscal 2030 (heading toward about half), and $150 billion of remaining performance obligations with fixed price floors and committed volumes.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Contracted backlog improves earnings visibility and cushions a downturn, but also shows customers fear shortages.
insights.locator: To secure supplies of memory and flash

insights.claim: Micron's CTO said the company is two generations ahead of China's CXMT, and the author expects Micron to keep that lead to stop customers moving to Chinese memory.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Technology lead is the moat versus Chinese entrants; watch CXMT node and yield progress.
insights.locator: Micron's chief technology officer, Scott DeBoer

insights.claim: CXMT listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in July and raised $8.6 billion, small relative to rivals' profits, but the author thinks China is dead serious about supplying its own memory and selling globally.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Chinese memory supply is a medium-term threat to the pricing regime and a geopolitical factor.
insights.quote: It is only a matter of time.
insights.locator: CXMT just went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange

themes.theme: HBM as a historic profit pool

insights.claim: The author argues HBM stacked DRAM may be the most profitable product in six decades of commercial IT, rivaling IBM mainframe engines of the 1970s, and that advanced packaging is central to that value.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Value is accruing to memory and advanced packaging, not just GPU designers.
insights.locator: It may turn out that HBM stacked DRAM

insights.claim: Without the stacked high bandwidth DRAM made by Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix, the GenAI revolution could not have happened, and HBM underpins Nvidia and AMD growth.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: GPU growth depends on HBM supply, giving memory vendors bargaining power over accelerator makers.
insights.locator: And no matter what, the growth of the HBM market

insights.claim: The author estimates a 12-high HBM stack weighs about a quarter gram and costs $500 to $600, implying $62,500 to $75,000 per troy ounce versus gold at $4,176, so HBM4 is worth 15X to 18X gold by weight.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Illustrative estimate (not company data) of HBM value density.
insights.locator: Which brings me to my final point
